headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via Haystack MCP/REST ingestion into Botpress workflows; capability overlap also creates cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content that Botpress may later consume in chatbot flows. Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls here, so prompt-like content can traverse the pair. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests untrusted MCP or REST content and forwards it into Botpress prompts or knowledge inputs, injection is possible.
IF Botpress treats retrieved file or message content as trusted instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Haystack outputs before Botpress consumes them.
Restrict Botpress to a fixed instruction template that ignores embedded directives.
Disable MCP sources that are not allowlisted.
Review one end-to-end prompt path with a malicious test string.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the integration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, while Botpress is a support bot that may process user content. If they share a workspace or pass files through the same integration, sensitive content can be transmitted outward by Haystack. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Botpress and Haystack share files, transcripts, or embeddings in one workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Haystack sends retrieved context to third-party APIs, any Botpress-processed sensitive content can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Remove secrets and PII from shared inputs.
Route Haystack through a local-only backend for one test run.
Audit outbound destinations for Haystack.
Separate Botpress and Haystack workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Haystack can use MCP and broad egress, but neither profile shows shared write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database. That makes direct write-write conflict plausible only under unusual orchestration. Uncertainty remains because the profiles omit locking and workspace details, so the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one git checkout without locks, concurrent mutation becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Disable package installation during shared runs.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Check whether both agents target the same mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent and Botpress is a customer-support agent, so a common pattern is Haystack retrieving content that Botpress then uses in responses. Without documented verification or provenance checks, Botpress may treat Haystack output as authoritative. The pair therefore has a default cascade path, though the exact workflow is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Haystack output is fed into Botpress response generation without a verification step, errors can cascade.
IF Botpress executes downstream actions based on Haystack facts, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require Botpress to cite source snippets before acting.
Add a human review step for high-impact responses.
Compare Haystack answers against a second source for critical tasks.
Log retrieval provenance end to end.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics, while Botpress has no data-class disclosure here. That creates a small compliance gap around telemetry and retention, but no PHI, EU PII, or residency mismatch is documented. Because the profiles are sparse, I cannot rule out broader compliance issues, so I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data through Haystack telemetry, compliance obligations may expand.
IF Botpress stores support transcripts containing personal data, retention policy alignment becomes necessary.
mitigations: Disable telemetry for regulated deployments.
Classify data handled by Botpress before enabling Haystack.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Review privacy notices for support transcripts.
requires-engineering: document a shared data-processing agreement and residency policy.
